## ⭐ Extra Credit at a Glance

Life on Earth started as tiny **microbes** (basically slime!) more than 3.5 billion years ago. It took about **4 billion years** to get to animals. Along the way, Earth almost froze, filled up with oxygen, and survived huge disasters. How did Earth stay a good home for life the whole time?

# Part 1: The Faint Young Sun {#part-1}

<a class="ab-connects" href="#q1">Helps with Question 1</a>

### ☀️ The Sun used to be dimmer

The Sun makes energy by squeezing **hydrogen** together to make **helium** in its core. This is called **fusion**.

- When 4 hydrogen bits join into 1 helium bit, the core ends up with **fewer particles**.
- With fewer particles, the core gets **squeezed** by the weight of the Sun above it.
- A squeezed core gets **hotter**, so fusion goes **faster**, and the Sun shines **brighter**.

This has been happening for the Sun's whole life. So the young Sun was about **25–30% dimmer** than it is today.

### 🥶 So why didn't Earth freeze?

With a dimmer Sun, early Earth should have been a giant ice ball. But rocks show that Earth had **liquid water** at least **3.8 billion years ago**. Scientists call this puzzle the **faint young Sun paradox.**

The best answer: early Earth had a **stronger greenhouse effect.** Its air had much more **greenhouse gas**, which trapped more heat:

- **Carbon dioxide (CO₂)** was much higher than today.
- **Methane (CH₄)** was much, much higher. Today oxygen in the air destroys methane, but early Earth had **almost no oxygen**, so methane made by microbes could build up.

This thick **"greenhouse shield"** of CO₂ and methane kept the oceans from freezing.

### 🔥 Try it: Sun vs. greenhouse

Slide back in time. Watch the Sun get dimmer, and see how much **extra** greenhouse warming Earth would need to stay as warm as today.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof abSunGa = Inputs.range([0, 4.5], {value: 3.5, step: 0.5, label: "Billions of years ago:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const t0 = 4.57;
  const L = 1 / (1 + 0.4 * (1 - (t0 - abSunGa) / t0));   // Gough (1981) model of the Sun's brightness
  const bareC = 255 * Math.pow(L, 0.25) - 273.15;         // Earth with no atmosphere
  const needed = 15 - bareC;                               // greenhouse warming needed to stay at 15 °C
  const extra = needed - 33;                               // beyond today's 33 °C greenhouse effect
  const pct = Math.round(L * 100);
  const sunR = 30 + 40 * L;
  return html`<div style="background:#0b1d3a;color:#fff;border-radius:16px;padding:18px;max-width:${Math.min(width, 600)}px;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">
    <div style="display:flex;gap:18px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;">
      <svg width="110" height="110" viewBox="0 0 120 120" role="img" aria-label="Sun drawn at ${pct}% of today's brightness">
        <defs><radialGradient id="abSunGrad"><stop offset="0%" stop-color="#fff7cc"/><stop offset="70%" stop-color="#fbbf24"/><stop offset="100%" stop-color="#f59e0b" stop-opacity="0"/></radialGradient></defs>
        <circle cx="60" cy="60" r="${sunR}" fill="url(#abSunGrad)" opacity="${0.45 + 0.55 * L}"/>
      </svg>
      <div style="flex:1;min-width:190px;line-height:1.7;">
        <div style="font-size:1.5em;font-weight:800;">Sun: ${pct}% as bright as today</div>
        <div>${extra < 1 ? "Today's greenhouse effect is enough. 👍" : html`Earth needs about <b style="color:#fca5a5;">${Math.round(extra)} °C more</b> greenhouse warming than today to keep its oceans liquid.`}</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>`;
}
```

*This is a simple model based on how scientists think the Sun's brightness has changed.*

::: {.ab-key-idea}
🔑 **Big idea:** The young Sun was dimmer because the Sun gets brighter as fusion squeezes and heats its core. Earth stayed warm anyway because **lots of CO₂ and methane** trapped extra heat.
:::

# Part 2: Earth's Thermostat {#part-2}

<a class="ab-connects" href="#q2">Helps with Question 2</a>

A **thermostat** keeps a house from getting too hot or too cold. Earth has a natural thermostat too. It's called the **carbonate–silicate cycle**, and it controls how much **CO₂** is in the air.

### 🔄 How the cycle works

1. **Rain pulls CO₂ out of the air.** CO₂ mixes into rainwater, and the rain slowly breaks down (weathers) rocks on land.
2. **Rivers carry the carbon to the ocean.** There it gets stored in seafloor rock called **limestone.** Now the carbon is **sequestered** (locked away).
3. **Plate tectonics moves the seafloor.** Ocean plates slowly slide **under** other plates. This is called **subduction.**
4. **Volcanoes send CO₂ back into the air.** Deep underground, heat and pressure break down the limestone, and **volcanoes** release the CO₂.

Without plate tectonics, step 4 would never happen. Rain would keep pulling CO₂ out of the air until Earth **froze.**

### 🌡️ Try it: Watch the thermostat work

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof abThermo = Inputs.radio(["🔥 Earth gets too warm", "❄️ Earth gets too cold"], {value: "🔥 Earth gets too warm", label: "What happens if…"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const warm = abThermo.startsWith("🔥");
  const steps = warm
    ? ["Earth heats up", "More rain falls", "Rain breaks down rocks faster", "More CO₂ gets pulled out of the air", "Less greenhouse gas", "Earth cools back down ✅"]
    : ["Earth cools down", "Less rain falls", "Rocks break down slower", "Volcanoes keep adding CO₂, so it builds up", "More greenhouse gas", "Earth warms back up ✅"];
  const color = warm ? "#ef4444" : "#3b82f6";
  const node = document.createElement("div");
  node.style.cssText = `max-width:${Math.min(width, 600)}px;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;`;
  node.innerHTML = steps.map((s, i) => `
    <div class="ab-thermo-step" style="opacity:0;transition:opacity .4s ${i * 0.4}s;">
      <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;background:${color}1a;border:2px solid ${color};border-radius:10px;padding:10px 14px;">
        <span style="background:${color};color:#fff;font-weight:800;border-radius:50%;min-width:30px;height:30px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;">${i + 1}</span>
        <b>${s}</b>
      </div>
      ${i < steps.length - 1 ? `<div style="text-align:center;color:${color};font-size:1.3em;line-height:1.4;" aria-hidden="true">⬇</div>` : ""}
    </div>`).join("");
  requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(() =>
    node.querySelectorAll(".ab-thermo-step").forEach(el => el.style.opacity = 1)));
  return node;
}
```

::: {.ab-key-idea}
🔑 **Big idea:** The cycle is a **negative feedback loop.** If Earth gets too warm, it pulls out more CO₂ and cools down. If Earth gets too cold, CO₂ builds up and warms it. This keeps Earth in the range where water stays **liquid.** (It's very slow, though. It takes about a million years, so it can't fix today's climate change.)
:::

# Part 3: Oxygen, Ice, and Big Changes for Life {#part-3}

<a class="ab-connects" href="#q3">Helps with Question 3</a> <a class="ab-connects" href="#visual-task">Helps with the graph</a>

### 💨 Oxygen arrives (slowly!)

- For Earth's first 2 billion years, the air had **almost no oxygen.** This is the **Anoxic Era** (4.5–2.4 Ga).
- **Cyanobacteria** were making oxygen by about **2.7 Ga.** But at first, the oxygen got used up right away. Much of it reacted with **iron** in the ocean, making rusty, striped rocks called **banded iron formations (BIFs).**
- Around **2.4 Ga**, oxygen finally started to build up in the air. This is the **Great Oxidation Event.** Oxygen rose to a **low** level (about 1% of the air), and an **ozone layer** formed to block harmful UV light.
- Then, for about a billion years (**1.8–0.8 Ga**), not much changed. Scientists call it the **"boring billion."** Still, **eukaryotic cells** (complex cells) had appeared by about **1.9 Ga**.
- From about **0.75 to 0.58 Ga**, oxygen rose a **second time**, high enough for animals.
- Around **0.54 Ga**, the **Cambrian Explosion** happened: lots of new animals appeared, many with shells and skeletons.
- Around **0.4 Ga**, plants spread across land and oxygen rose close to today's level (**Phanerozoic peak**). Today the air is **21% oxygen.**

<div class="ab-video">
<iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/qERdL8uHSgI" title="PBS Eons: That Time Oxygen Almost Killed Everything" loading="lazy" allow="accelerometer; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen></iframe>
</div>

*🎬 Optional video: PBS Eons, "That Time Oxygen Almost Killed Everything."*

### 🧗 Two hurdles on the way to animals

To go from single-celled microbes to animals, life had to clear **two big hurdles**:

1. **Complex cells (eukaryotic cells).** Simple microbe cells can't turn into many kinds of cells. Eukaryotic cells **can**, like muscle cells, brain cells, and skin cells. Every animal is built from them.
2. **Enough oxygen.** Animals need lots of **energy** to grow big and move. Using oxygen to get energy from food gives about **10 times more energy** than living without oxygen. Animals needed oxygen to be at least about **3% of the air.** That didn't happen until the second rise of oxygen, around **0.58 Ga.**

### 🧊 Snowball Earth

Twice, Earth may have frozen over almost completely, even at the equator. These are called **Snowball Earth** episodes:

::: {.ab-table-wrap}
| Snowball Earth | When | What happened at about the same time? |
|---|---|---|
| #1 | about **2.4–2.2 Ga** | The **Great Oxidation Event** |
| #2 | about **0.72–0.63 Ga** | The **second rise of oxygen** |
:::

**Why did Earth freeze?** When oxygen rose, it destroyed a lot of the **methane** greenhouse gas, so Earth cooled. Once ice spread, the shiny ice **reflected** sunlight, which made Earth even colder.

**How did it melt?** **Volcanoes** kept pumping out CO₂. With everything frozen, there was no rain to remove it. After a few million years, the CO₂ trapped enough heat to melt the ice.

### 🍾 Disasters as "bottlenecks"

A **bottleneck** is a crisis that wipes out most life, leaving only a few survivors. The survivors then spread out and evolve into **new kinds of life.** Earth's history shows this pattern again and again:

- **Oxygen and Snowball Earth:** Oxygen was **poison** to many early microbes, and the ice was brutal. But after each crisis, life came back **more complex.** After Snowball #1 came more oxygen and complex cells. After Snowball #2 came the **first animals** and the **Cambrian Explosion.**
- **Mass extinctions:** About **252 million years ago**, giant volcanic eruptions killed up to **95%** of ocean species. About **66 million years ago**, a 10-km **asteroid** hit Mexico and wiped out the dinosaurs. With the dinosaurs gone, **mammals** (including our ancestors) took over.

::: {.ab-key-idea}
🔑 **Big idea:** Life on Earth is **resilient** (tough). Disasters wiped out lots of life, but they also **cleared the way** for new and more complex life to evolve.
:::

# Part 4: What Earth Teaches Us About Aliens {#part-4}

<a class="ab-connects" href="#q4">Helps with Question 4</a>

### 🛸 The Drake Equation

In 1961, astronomer **Frank Drake** made an equation to estimate how many alien civilizations might be out there. It multiplies a list of factors together. Your question focuses on two of them:

::: {.ab-table-wrap}
| Factor | What it means (in your assignment) | What Earth's history tells us |
|---|---|---|
| **f~c~** | The fraction of planets with life where **complex animal life** develops | On Earth, it took about **4 billion years** to build up enough oxygen for animals. Microbes had Earth to themselves for most of that time. On another planet it could take **even longer**, maybe longer than its star lasts. So complex life might be **rare**, even if microbes are common. |
| **L** | How long a **technological civilization** lasts | Big disasters keep happening. Earth gets hit by a dinosaur-killing-size asteroid about **every 100 million years.** A civilization could be wiped out by bad luck, so **L might be short.** |
:::

::: {.ab-key-idea}
🔑 **Big idea:** Earth shows that **simple life is tough** and can survive almost anything. But **complex life takes a long time** to appear, and **civilizations may not last long.** Both of these make the number of aliens we could talk to **smaller.**
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🤓 Fun fact for extra-curious students
In Drake's original equation, f~c~ means something a little different: the fraction of intelligent aliens that build technology we could detect, like radio. For this assignment, use the meaning in the table above.
:::

|---|---|---|
| 4.5 – 2.4 | **Anoxic Era.** Faint young Sun; CO₂ + methane greenhouse shield keeps oceans liquid | Almost none (Anoxic) |
| about 3.8 – 1.8 | **Banded iron formations** form as oxygen reacts with iron in the ocean | |
| about 2.7 | **Cyanobacteria** making oxygen | Still almost none |
| 2.4 | **Great Oxidation Event** | Jumps to Low |
| 2.4 – 2.2 | **Snowball Earth #1** | Low |
| about 1.9 | **Eukaryotic cells** | Low |
| 1.8 – 0.8 | **"Boring billion"** | Low and flat |
| 0.72 – 0.63 | **Snowball Earth #2** | Starting to rise |
| 0.75 – 0.58 | **Second rise of oxygen** | Rises to High |
| 0.54 | **Cambrian Explosion** of animals | High |
| 0.4 – 0 | Plants on land; **Phanerozoic peak** | High (near today's 21%) |
:::

## Visual Task: Oxygen Graph & Timeline {#visual-task}

::: {.ab-task}
Draw a graph of **oxygen in the air vs. time**, from 4.5 Ga to today. Add labels for the big events.

**Your graph needs:**

- **X-axis:** Time in billions of years ago: 4.5, 3.5, 2.5, 1.5, 0.5, 0 Ga.
- **Y-axis:** Oxygen level: **Anoxic → Low → High.**
- **The line:** Show the Anoxic Era (4.5–2.4 Ga), the Great Oxidation Event (2.4 Ga), the second rise (0.75–0.58 Ga), and the Phanerozoic peak.

**Labels to add:**

1. **Faint Young Sun Era:** the CO₂/methane greenhouse shield that kept the oceans liquid.
2. **Life milestones:** cyanobacteria, eukaryotic cells, Cambrian Explosion.
3. **Disasters:** Snowball Earth #1 and #2, and banded iron formations.
:::

### ✅ Graph checklist

Tick each item as you add it to your graph.

```{=html}
<div id="ab-graph-check" style="font-family:Inter,sans-serif;"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  var items = [
    "Title, and both axes labeled",
    "Time numbers on the x-axis (4.5 on the LEFT, 0 on the RIGHT)",
    "Line starts near the bottom (Anoxic Era)",
    "Line steps up at 2.4 Ga (Great Oxidation Event)",
    "Line steps up again at 0.75–0.58 Ga (second rise) to High",
    "Label: Faint Young Sun / greenhouse shield",
    "Labels: cyanobacteria, eukaryotic cells, Cambrian Explosion",
    "Labels: Snowball Earth #1 and #2, banded iron formations"
  ];
  var KEY = "ab-graph-check-v2";
  var saved = [];
  try { saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || "[]") || []; } catch (e) { saved = []; }
  var root = document.getElementById("ab-graph-check");
  var count = document.createElement("div");
  count.style.cssText = "font-weight:700;margin:6px 0 10px;";
  function update() { var n = root.querySelectorAll("input:checked").length; count.textContent = n + " of " + items.length + " done" + (n === items.length ? " 🎉 Ready to turn in!" : ""); }
  root.appendChild(count);
  items.forEach(function (txt, i) {
    var lab = document.createElement("label");
    lab.className = "ab-check";
    var cb = document.createElement("input");
    cb.type = "checkbox";
    cb.checked = saved.indexOf(i) !== -1;
    cb.addEventListener("change", function () {
      saved = []; root.querySelectorAll("input").forEach(function (x, j) { if (x.checked) saved.push(j); });
      try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(saved)); } catch (e) {}
      update();
    });
    var span = document.createElement("span");
    span.textContent = txt;
    lab.appendChild(cb); lab.appendChild(span);
    root.appendChild(lab);
  });
  update();
})();
</script>
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 💡 Graph tips
- Oxygen went up in **steps**, with long flat parts. Draw it like stairs, not a smooth curve.
- Some events last a long time (banded iron formations, Snowball Earth). Show them as **shaded bars** under the line.
- Things get crowded near the right side. Use **arrows** to point to your labels.
:::

# Quick Practice {#practice}

Check that you understand before you write. This part is **not** turned in.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function abBuildQuiz(questions) {
  const outer = html`<div style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#0f766e 0%,#6d28d9 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:16px 22px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;">🧠 Quick Practice</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.85;margin-top:4px;">Pick an answer to see feedback.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #99f6e4;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;background:#f0fdfa;padding:14px;"></div>`;
  const scoreEl = html`<div style="font-weight:700;color:#134e4a;margin:4px 0 12px;">Score: 0 / ${questions.length}</div>`;
  let score = 0, done = 0;
  body.appendChild(scoreEl);
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 18px;margin-bottom:12px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi + 1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.92em;";
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.type = "button";
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;";
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if (card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "1";
        done++;
        const right = oi === qq.correct;
        if (right) score++;
        const buttons = card.querySelectorAll("button");
        buttons.forEach(b => { b.style.cursor = "default"; b.style.color = "#475569"; });
        buttons[qq.correct].style.borderColor = "#16a34a"; buttons[qq.correct].style.background = "#f0fdf4"; buttons[qq.correct].style.color = "#166534";
        if (!right) { btn.style.borderColor = "#dc2626"; btn.style.background = "#fef2f2"; btn.style.color = "#991b1b"; }
        fb.innerHTML = (right ? "✅ Correct! " : "❌ ") + qq.explanation;
        fb.style.cssText += `padding:10px 14px;margin-top:8px;color:${right ? "#166534" : "#991b1b"};background:${right ? "#f0fdf4" : "#fef2f2"};`;
        scoreEl.textContent = `Score: ${score} / ${questions.length}` + (done === questions.length ? (score >= 5 ? " 🌟 You're ready to write!" : " 📖 Reread the parts you missed.") : "");
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```
